title: How I Turn Cheap Ramen Into a $4 Gourmet Dinner With Peanut Butter
description: Skip the $25 takeout. This 10-minute spicy peanut butter ramen upgrade uses basic pantry staples for a creamy, restaurant-worthy meal at home.
story: Yesterday was one of those crazy work days where 8 PM rolled around and my fridge looked practically empty. I stared down a pack of cheap Top Ramen in my pantry and refused to drop twenty-five bucks on delivery again. Grabbing a jar of creamy peanut butter from my Aldi stash and a squirt of sriracha changed everything. The first time I tested this, I tossed the peanut butter straight into boiling water and it clumped up into a giant oily mess—total rookie mistake. Now, I whisk it right in the bowl with a splash of hot noodle water first, and it turns into the silkiest, creamiest sauce ever. It totally saved my Tuesday night, and my wallet is thanking me.
ingredients: 1 pack instant ramen noodles (any flavor, though chicken works best)
2 tablespoons creamy peanut butter (Trader Joe's or Jif)
1 teaspoon sriracha or chili garlic sauce
1/4 cup hot starchy water reserved from cooking the noodles
1 green onion, thinly sliced for topping
instructions: Step 1: Bring a small pot of water to a boil and cook your ramen noodles for about 3 minutes until tender. Do not add the flavor packet yet.

Step 2: While the noodles boil, grab a cereal bowl and whisk together the peanut butter, soy sauce, sriracha, sesame oil, minced garlic, and about half of the ramen seasoning packet until it forms a thick paste.
Step 3: Before draining the noodles, carefully scoop out 1/4 cup of that starchy cooking water. Whisk it directly into your peanut butter paste until it turns into a smooth, glossy sauce.
Step 4: Toss your cooked noodles right into the sauce, stir vigorously until everything is coated and steaming, then top with sliced green onions and dig in!
proHack: Always mix your peanut butter, soy sauce, and hot noodle water in the bowl first before adding the noodles. If you dump peanut butter straight into boiling liquid, it breaks apart and gets greasy instead of emulsifying into a creamy sauce.
storage: This is honestly best eaten immediately while the noodles are hot and saucy. If you have leftovers, store them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 day. Reheat on the stove with a tiny splash of water because the noodles will soak up all that peanut sauce overnight.

faqs.question: Can I substitute the peanut butter if I have a nut allergy?
faqs.answer: Totally! Sunflower seed butter (SunButter) or even tahini work as great allergy-friendly swaps with a very similar thick, nutty texture.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the sauce from getting too thick and clumpy?
faqs.answer: Don't skip the starchy cooking water step! That hot water is full of starches that help thin out the peanut butter so it coats the noodles evenly.
